truths.statement: Two independent gates control creator capability: a paid yearly subscription (Basic/Pro) unlocks uploading and creator tools, while manual KYC approval unlocks receiving earnings; a creator who has paid but has pending KYC can upload and sell but cannot be paid out yet, and that is a normal state, not an edge case.
Basic subscription tier grants 3 content uploads (1 free, 2 paid); Pro tier grants 7 content uploads (2 free, 5 paid).
The first upload from a given creator must be free, enforced server-side (rejecting a paid first submission), not merely suggested in the UI.
Basic-tier creators can host/moderate only open (general) communities; Pro-tier creators can additionally open and host private communities.
Reading messages in open/general communities is always free regardless of credit balance or trial status; only sending a message costs 1 credit.

There is no entry fee to publish content, DM, or host a community at the standard 85/15 split — eligibility alone (not payment) unlocks the standard tier of creator activity; paying for Basic/Pro only adds upload-count limits, community-hosting scope, and the upgraded 90/10 split.
Storefront/physical-product sales route entirely through the existing external WAWUBasket/WAWUBeauty apps as a handoff; the commerce engine for storefront is never rebuilt inside this product.

Pension registration and 1-month free health insurance perks are partnership dependencies requiring an actual signed agreement with a licensed pension fund administrator and an insurer respectively; no engineering effort can ship them without that partnership, and status must be confirmed before scoping build time.

The "free course(s)" perks (1 for Basic, up to 3 for Pro) assume access is granted into an existing training/course catalog (the app's `/training` section) rather than a new content library — this mapping needs confirmation, not assumption.

PPV content and downloadable content (video, course, audio, PDF/book, image/art, template) are priced ₦100–₦5,000 (currency adjusts by region), paid once for permanent stream/download access, split 85% creator / 15% WAWU standard.
Direct-message price is creator-set in the range ₦50–₦500 per message, split 85/15 to the creator on a timely response, with zero WAWU fee taken on a refunded (missed-deadline) message.
WAWU Credits are sold in three fixed prepaid packs: Starter ₦500 for 50 credits, Popular ₦1,000 for 120 credits, Pro ₦2,000 for 300 credits; split 90% creator / 10% WAWU per credit spent.

Creator Subscription pricing is fixed and annual: Basic ₦5,999/year, Pro ₦18,999/year; the subscription fee itself is 100% WAWU / 0% creator revenue (it is a fee creators pay WAWU, not a revenue-share item).

Standard revenue split across PPV/downloads, DM (on-time response), tips, and storefront is 85% creator / 15% WAWU; Pro-tier creators receive an upgraded 90% creator / 10% WAWU on those same streams (1, 2, 3, 5, 6) — this is the stated actual incentive to purchase Pro.

The WAWU Credits revenue split is 90% creator / 10% WAWU regardless of the creator's subscription tier (Basic or Pro) — it does not follow the standard-vs-Pro split rule that governs the other five streams.

A DirectMessage moves from `awaiting_response` to `responded` (creator paid 85/15 or 90/10) if the creator replies within 24 hours of `sentAt`, or to `refunded` (full user refund, zero WAWU fee) if a scheduled cron sweep finds it past `deadlineAt` (`sentAt + 24h`) still `awaiting_response`.

Each DM auto-refund event also updates the creator's rolling `noResponseRatePct`, which drives a `penaltyState` machine: none (<10%) → warned (10–30%) → disabled_7d (30–50%) → disabled_30d (>50%), with `dmDisabledUntil` set automatically when disabled.

Creator Subscription state moves active → past_due (on a failed annual renewal charge) → expired (after N failed retries per a defined backoff); on expiry, `commissionRateOverride` is cleared and all tier perks including the 90/10 split revert to standard.

Subscription renewal is an annual scheduled job that charges the stored `flutterwaveCustomerRef`; success extends `currentPeriodEnd` by 1 year, failure increments `renewalAttempts` and retries before the state transitions to past_due/expired.

Every new user gets an automatic 7-day free trial of community chat starting at signup (`trialEndsAt = signup + 7d`); after the trial, sending a community message requires a positive credit balance (reading remains free at all times, and credits are non-refundable once purchased).

A Purchase moves pending → completed | failed, and the server must re-verify the transaction against Flutterwave's API before marking it `completed` — the client-side payment callback alone is never trusted to finalize a purchase.

Submitted content starts in status `pending` until the existing moderation path (automated + manual review) clears it; once approved, free content goes fully live while approved paid content remains preview-only until the specific viewer has a completed Purchase for it.

KYC is manual-review only: a creator's payout eligibility passes through at least a pending state (paid-but-pending is an explicitly named normal state) before earnings can be released; there is no automated approval path.

A piece of content's `fullAssetUrl` is included in the API response only if the content is free OR the requester has a completed Purchase for that content id (short-lived signed URL either way); otherwise it is omitted and `fullAssetLocked: true` is returned instead, so client UI never needs the real asset URL to render the lock state.

EVG-lite is a single computed integer per creator, `evgScore = views + purchases × weight + comments`, where the purchase weight is a global config constant (not per-creator); it is surfaced only as a badge with no trend lines, percentile ranking, or insights engine.

`noResponseRatePct` is a rolling-window decimal computed per creator from missed-vs-total DM deadlines; the locked thresholds mapping it to `penaltyState` are <10% → none, 10–30% → warned, 30–50% → disabled_7d, >50% → disabled_30d.

No endpoint, admin action, or support-tool script may ever convert a user's `creditBalance` back into a Flutterwave payout or naira value — doing so breaks the boundary that keeps Credits out of wallet/e-money-licensing territory; any future request to add this must be stopped and flagged, not built.

No wallet, cash balance, or withdrawal UI exists or is being built anywhere in the product; the mechanism by which creators actually receive their 85–90% share is an explicitly out-of-scope, separate business/ops decision, not part of this build.

WAWU Credits must render in the UI purely as a count (e.g. "48 credits"), never displayed or implied as a naira value — a display-layer invariant reinforcing (but distinct from) the non-cashable rule.

Credits are single-purpose: they can be spent only on messages in general/open communities, never on PPV, downloads, DMs, tips, or anything else; any request to broaden credit usage is the wallet problem re-appearing and must be flagged, not implemented.
Creator is an account type chosen at signup or via upgrade, not a trust-tier badge earned by climbing a ladder — the earlier "trust-tier-based creator gate" model is explicitly wrong and replaced.
No DRM or screenshot/recording-block claims exist anywhere in the product or its UI copy — not achievable on the web platform at any budget or timeline.

No automated identity verification (liveness check, Face ID) exists or is being built; KYC is entirely manual (BVN + NIN for Nigeria, national-ID equivalent elsewhere, plus ID document and payout bank details) — a stale "Face-ID liveness check" string in the old `src/lib/profile-data.ts` is dead display copy and must be ignored.

Live streaming is phased out of the current build; pre-recorded video covers the PPV-video need for now, and any change to pull real-time ingest/playback/live-chat forward must be confirmed before scoping.

Event Tickets, Jobs/gigs/recruiting (including the word "gigs" anywhere in copy — the Pro perk is "Recommended Deals," not "Recommended Gigs & Deals"), Blockchain/NFT, and Admin AML/CFT compliance dashboards are all cut entirely and must not be silently reintroduced.

There is no Jobs section, Gigs section, Event Tickets section, Opportunities section, or Events section anywhere in this product — consistent with 01_SPEC.md's cut of Event Tickets and Jobs/gigs/recruiting.

DM disputes, content moderation, and subscription-status views must extend the existing admin moderation/audit-trail system (ban/suspend logging, `trust_audit`/`moderation_log` export types) rather than building a second/parallel admin or dispute system.

Every one-time-payment stream (PPV, downloads, DM, tips, Credits) reuses the exact existing Flutterwave inline-checkout call pattern already live for CAC/NEPC payments; recurring billing for Creator Subscriptions rides the same underlying Flutterwave gateway relationship via its recurring-charge capability — no new PCI scope is introduced, and WAWU never touches raw card data.

A Purchase's `commissionRate` is snapshotted at the moment of purchase (0.15 standard, or 0.10 if the creator was Pro-tier-and-active at that instant) and does not retroactively change if the creator's subscription tier changes afterward.

There is no platform-wide consumer subscription in this model — fans pay creators directly per-item (PPV, downloads, DMs, tips, credits) rather than subscribing to the platform itself; the locked model is structurally closer to Passes.com's fan-to-creator mechanic than earlier drafts, intentionally simplified (no $29/mo creator SaaS fee, no flat per-transaction surcharge).

docs/01_SPEC.md §6 declares the trust-tier-based creator gate "wrong — replaced" by the account-type + subscription + manual-KYC model, yet docs/01_SPEC.md §7 and docs/03_USER_FLOWS.md §B1 still describe creator eligibility to publish/DM/host as gated by the legacy trust tier (`certified_professional`/`trusted_partner`, "same gate the composer already uses"), and docs/02_TECHNICAL_CONTEXT.md §3.1 has the publish endpoint reject requests where "requester's trust tier isn't certified_professional/trusted_partner" — the docs are not fully reconciled on which gate is authoritative for publishing; treat CLAUDE.md's locked two-gate model (subscription unlocks uploading, KYC unlocks earning, creator = account type) as the tiebreaker for gating logic, but flag the trust-tier check in §3.1 as a discrepancy to resolve, not silently implement as an additional undocumented gate.

docs/02_TECHNICAL_CONTEXT.md §4 ("Frontend — files to touch") references a pre-rebuild file structure (`src/lib/posts.ts`, `src/lib/feed-data.ts`, `src/lib/adapt.ts`, `src/app/(feed)/create/[category]/page.tsx`) that does not match the actual current repo, which lives under `src/app/(app)/`, `src/app/create/`, and `src/lib/api/` per CLAUDE.md; Section 4's file paths are stale and must be ignored for implementation, but Sections 1–3 of the same doc (data model and `/api/hub/...` API contract shapes: Purchase, DirectMessage, Credits, Subscription, EVG-lite field lists) remain the authoritative target contract and should be treated as strong evidence, not mere inference from screens.

docs/01_SPEC.md §7 and docs/02_TECHNICAL_CONTEXT.md §4 describe the "actual" current bottom nav as Home / Market / Create / Opportunities / More (5 slots, with a live Opportunities tab for jobs/grants/funding), which conflicts with CLAUDE.md's locked current nav of Home / Communities / [Explore|Create] / Messages / Profile with no Opportunities or Market slot; the docs describe a pre-rebuild nav state that CLAUDE.md's locked nav has since superseded, so CLAUDE.md's nav is current truth, not the SPEC/technical-context doc's described nav.

docs/01_SPEC.md §0 frames this feature as "Built on top of the existing WAWU feed/post/profile system... Not a new app, not a new IA," reusing existing trust tiers and upload infra, while CLAUDE.md (the current, authoritative project instructions) describes the whole project as a "Ground-up rebuild — it replaces the old post-feed app entirely"; CLAUDE.md's ground-up-rebuild framing is current truth, so 01_SPEC.md's "reuse the existing app/IA" framing should be read as superseded context — its locked monetization numbers and mechanics (Section 1 table, splits, prices, DM/Credits rules) remain valid target-state truth regardless.

A Pro-tier creator's 90/10 split applies specifically to streams 1 (PPV), 2 (downloads), 3 (DM, on response), 5 (tips), and 6 (storefront) — Credits (stream 4) is excluded from the tier-based split upgrade because it is fixed at 90/10 for all creators regardless of tier.
